newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends lower in local-dominated trade.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends lower in local-dominated trade.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures ended broadly lower in sluggish dealings on Thursday, pressured by local and speculative selling, dealers said.
"Not that much really happened today," said one dealer. "It was really a local-dominated market. Volume was 7,820 lots and about half of that was locals."
September cocoa fell $25 per tonne on the day, to $1,513, after ranging between $1,542 and $1,510. Second-month December closed $25 lower, at $1,560, while the back months also finished down $25.

The cocoa market fell at the opening, as expected, after a weak performance in the London market overnight. But CSCE September's failure initially to get past chart support at $1,519-$1,521 prompted a bout of local short-covering, traders said.
The spot contract briefly traded above unchanged, but reversed again after buying dried up, dealers said. Downward momentum picked up after September breached $1,519-$1,521 support.

On the charts, traders now pegged September support at the day's low of $1,510, with some psychological support noted at $1,500. Subsequent downside hurdles were put at $1,485 and $,1475. On the upside, resistance was seen at $1,547-$1,550, followed by a gap between $1,561 and $1,570.
After bouncing sharply on both sides of unchanged this week. Traders said the market appeared to be stuck in a range between $1,485 and $1,550 basis September.
Some traders said the market could come under some pressure going into September first notice day on August 18.
September open interest as of July 30, stood at 23,698 lots, up 92 lots from the previous session.
